findings.title: High-case stack load at the 5 V pin comes within about 0.02-0.10 A of the 0.63 A minimum port current limit.
findings.what: All Frontend and FPGA-LDO power enters on one HDMI contact, J3.19, and passes through U16. Each HDMI port on the HDMI Extension Board has a TPS2553 switch that holds current constant at its limit; U16 is a buck converter, so if its input sags it draws more current, which can brown out or cycle the stack. Built up from the project's per-rail estimate, the load is comfortably below the limit in the expected case but close to it in the high case with all stimulators on, and the LDO board's +/-12 V start-up surge will briefly hit the limit at every power-up. No Vivado power figure or measurement exists, so the files cannot settle this; a measurement on the first Frontend + FPGA-LDO stack can.
findings.where: Frontend J3.19 VIN_5V (TP14) -> U16 -> VIN_3V3, which also leaves on J2 pins 68-70 to the FPGA-LDO board; HDMI Extension Board TPS2553 port switches U701-U708 with ILIM resistors R711-R718 = 37.4k.
findings.evidence: The 'about 0.55 A' in U16's Rated_output_current field (exports/frontend/parts.csv) is the old whole-system allowance at 3.3 V (about 0.43 A at 5 V; overnight hand-off C17, routing hand-off line 85), so adding the LDO board's 155-215 mA to it counts that board twice. Rebuilt from inputs/hdmi/power_estimate/START_HERE.md Frontend-only rows (0.23 A expected, 0.42 A high at 3.3 V) plus the LDO board's 155-215 mA (parts review V21), with 3.315 V / (0.88 x 4.8 V) = 0.785 A at 5 V per A at 3.3 V: about 0.30-0.35 A expected and 0.48-0.50 A high at the 5 V pin. Full stimulation (8 x 128 x 22.5 uA = 23 mA, about 15 mA above the 8 mA already budgeted) adds about 0.05-0.11 A, giving 0.53-0.61 A high. LDO board start-up inrush: 0.5-1 A at 3.3 V for 1-2 ms. Port limit at 37.4k: 637 / 696 / 764 mA min / nom / max, about 630-771 mA with the 1% resistor. The 88% efficiency is assumed, not read from the curves. The J3 contact rating (0.8 A, Molex catalog) was not verified; another source gives 0.3 A (separate finding).
findings.source: TI TPS2553 SLVS841G, eq. 1-3 (pp16-17) and section 8.5.1 (equations as read by other reviewers; the TI PDF text could not be decoded in this check); MPM3833C Rev 1.0 efficiency curves (not re-read); engineering judgement.
findings.consequence: In the high case, ports may enter current limit and the stack may brown out or fail to start. The limit cannot simply be raised, because its maximum is already near the J3 contact rating, so a fix could mean a cable, board or power-architecture change.
findings.suggested_action: Get a Vivado report_power or XPE figure and measure the first Frontend + FPGA-LDO stack at TP14, including start-up with the +/-12 V converter, before fixing R711-R718 and ordering eight stacks.

findings.title: Two out-of-stock parts are feedback resistors (R10, R13); building without them drives GTP rails above absolute max.
findings.what: R7, R10 and R13 have no JLC stock and are the upper feedback resistors (output to FB pin) of U4, U5 and U6. If the order is built with these lines not placed, each lower resistor holds FB at 0 V and the regulator drives its output toward its input. MGTAVCC and MGTAVTT, the FPGA transceiver supplies, would then rise to about 1.35-1.4 V, above their 1.10 V and 1.32 V absolute maximums. VCCO_1V5 would rise to about 3.3 V; that is within the bank's 3.6 V absolute maximum, but it puts 3.3 V levels on 1.5 V lines to the ASIC boards, and U4's power-good stays low, holding U6 off and the FPGA in reset.

findings.title: The Frontend uses the commercial 0-85 C FPGA by the owner's choice, and no thermal estimate shows it stays below 85 C.
findings.what: The JLC BOM places JLC part C1521720, which the project record identifies as the commercial XC7A35T-2CSG325C (junction limit 85 C); the schematic names the industrial -2CSG325I (100 C). The 22.59 x 25.42 mm Frontend dissipates about 0.9 W at the expected load and about 1.6 W in the high case, and its bottom face sits 1.5 mm above the FPGA-LDO board. Simple still-air screens give a rise of roughly 35-55 K at expected load and up to about 85 K in the high case for the board on its own; heat shared with the stack lowers this and the close facing board raises it. The junction could pass 85 C in the high case or in a warm head-worn environment; the files cannot settle this, and an XPE figure plus a thermocouple test on a heated stack would.
findings.where: Frontend U1 (top, 116.22, 113.0); regulators U2/U3/U4/U13 near the west edge and U16 at the north-east corner (122.74, 98.55); the whole Option A head stack.

findings.title: With C4 now not fitted, VCCINT is under the MPM3833C's 100 uF maximum, but MPS has not confirmed the remaining output capacitance and feed-forward capacitor.
findings.what: The MPM3833C datasheet lists 10 uF minimum, 22 uF typical and 100 uF maximum output capacitance, measured at one test point (1.2 V out, 2 A) on engineering samples. The module uses constant-on-time control (each switching pulse lasts a fixed time), and too much output capacitance can make its load-step response unstable. U2 on VCCINT has 186 uF fitted, still about 140-150 uF after the capacitors lose value under DC voltage, and also has a 22 pF feed-forward capacitor (C3, output to FB) that the MPS circuit does not show. VCCAUX (144 uF nominal) is borderline after derating, while VCCO and VIN_3V3 are probably below 100 uF effective; MPS does not show that any of these combinations is stable.

findings.title: Four MPM3833C modules use 0603 input capacitors and have no added SW copper, against the maker's layout guide.
findings.what: The MPM3833C buck module datasheet asks for an 0805 ceramic input capacitor as close to the pins as possible, wired directly to IN and PGND, and for extra copper on the SW (switch-node) pin to carry heat away. On U2, U3, U4 and U13 the input capacitors are 22 uF 0603 parts about 1.8 mm from the IN pin, and the SW pads have no copper beyond the pad itself. A smaller ceramic capacitor loses more of its capacitance under DC voltage (DC bias), so the 0603 parts give less effective capacitance at 3.3 V. The direct capacitor-to-IN/PGND connection is in place, and U16 already uses 0805 capacitors.
findings.where: Frontend FPGA Board, L1. U2 (VCCINT), U3 (VCCAUX), U4 (VCCO_1V5), U13 (1V4_GTP_IN) with input capacitors C1, C12, C21, C85 (22 uF 0603, GRM188R60J226). SW pads (Pad5/15) of these modules. U16 (5 V to 3.3 V) with C207 and C206 (0805) for comparison.
findings.evidence: exports/frontend/pads.csv and board.json: capacitor pad centre to IN pin C1 1.81, C12 1.77, C21 1.80, C85 1.81 mm; U16: C207 1.49, C206 2.09 mm. SW nets 'unconnected-(Ux-SW-Pad5/15)': 0 tracks, 0 zones. IN and PGND/AGND joined to the capacitor pads by 0.35-0.45 mm L1 tracks. Each pin 1 and pin 16 has one 0.1 mm L1-L2 GND microvia; each capacitor GND pad adds two (three at C207). exports/frontend/zones.csv: L2 GND 464 mm2 in one piece, 0.071 mm below L1. exports/frontend/parts.csv: C1/C12/C21/C85 C_0603 GRM188R60J226; C206/C207 C_0805 GRM21BR61A226.

findings.title: Most ASIC lanes that change layer at J2 have no ground via stack within 3 mm to carry their return current.
findings.what: When a signal changes layer through a via, its return current must also move between the ground planes next to each layer; a ground via close by gives it a short path. At J2, 34 lanes on L8 and L10 drop to L14 through a buried via plus laser microvias, so their return must move from the inner ground planes (L7, L9, L11) to L13; the 24 L12 lanes keep L13 as one reference, so only about half their return has to move. The only full ground via stack in the J2 field is north of the pins, so most of these returns detour 3 to 7 mm and share that detour, which breaks the project's own rule G05. The lanes are 32 MHz LVCMOS15 with default slow slew, so the effect is extra noise and crosstalk rather than a likely failure.
findings.where: Frontend, J2 field x 102.2-107.5 mm, y 104.4-121.9 mm. Worst lanes: /ASIC5_DATA4 (103.02, 117.4) L10->L14 6.84 mm; /ASIC5_DATA2 6.60 mm; BOARD3_SPI_CLK L8 6.49 mm; /ASIC3_CLK32MHz_Out L10 4.98 mm; /ASIC1_CLK32MHz_Out L8 4.52 mm; /ASIC5_CLK32MHz_Out L12 3.92 mm; STIM_CLK_SHARED L8 3.39 mm. J2 GND pins 14, 15, 27, 34, 41, 50, 66 each have one L13-L14 microvia only.
findings.evidence: exports/frontend/board.json vias (a review working file (not published), re-run independently): J2 has 58 lane transitions, 55 over 2 mm and 48 over 3 mm from the nearest full GND stack; median 5.08 mm on L8 (13 lanes), 5.17 mm on L10 (21), 3.26 mm on L12 (24). J1 by the same measure: maximum 2.25 mm. All 55 GND buried vias are in full stacks (4-11 + 11-12 + 12-13); in the J2 field the only one is at (106.0, 104.4), next nearest (108.0, 112.4), (109.42, 114.2), (110.22, 116.6), (109.42, 119.8). Distance from J2 GND pins to the nearest stack: 1.81 to 6.35 mm. zones.csv: GND planes on L2, L7, L9, L11, L13; no GND on L12 or L14. XDC: J2 nets LVCMOS15, no SLEW or DRIVE. Estimated extra return inductance a few tenths of a nH per lane (textbook via-pair formula, L11-L13 cavity 0.172 mm).
findings.source: Project routing ground rules V1, G05 (inputs/frontend/routing_rules/ROUTING_GROUND_RULES_V1.md, line 15): a signal via needs a nearby, connected ground-return transition. G05 gives no distance; the 1 to 1.5 mm target, and the J1 side showing about 1.2 mm is achievable, are engineering judgement.
findings.consequence: Lanes, including returned 32 MHz clocks and SPI clocks, share a longer return path, adding ground bounce, crosstalk and radiated noise near the ASIC connector; with no ASIC edge-rate data, a glitch at bring-up cannot be ruled out. It is cheap to fix now and hard after the boards are built.
findings.suggested_action: Before ordering, add full GND via stacks (L13 up through the buried via) beside the J2 GND pins and in the J2 via rows where room allows, then re-run the same return-distance check aiming for under 1 to 1.5 mm.

findings.title: Bottom decoupling caps reach ground only via L13, a median 1.6 mm (up to 3.9 mm) from a full ground stack.
findings.what: Decoupling capacitors on the bottom under the FPGA have a good via from the supply pad up to the supply plane, but the ground pad has only a single microvia (a tiny laser-drilled via) down to L13. L13 reaches the other ground planes (L2, L7, L9, L11) only through 55 full ground stacks, so each capacitor's current must run sideways on L13 to the nearest stack. That longer path adds loop inductance, which makes the capacitor less effective at high frequency. The added inductance is modest, about 0.5-0.8 nH per capacitor, not a failure.
findings.where: Frontend, bottom side, under U1. Worst: C55 (MGTAVTT, 470 nF) 3.86 mm; C54 and C56 (MGTAVTT) 3.20 mm; C52 (MGTAVCC) 2.96 mm; C18 (VCCAUX) 2.85 mm; C51 2.76 mm; C5 (VCCINT, 4.7 uF) 2.52 mm. Ground pad microvias L14-L13.
findings.evidence: exports/frontend/board.json: every GND buried via (2-3, 3-4, 4-11, 11-12, 12-13) is one of the same 55 stacks joining L2 to L13; 239 GND vias 1-2 and 163 GND vias 13-14 (155 alone). zones.csv: GND pours on L2, L7, L9, L11, L13; none on L14. Of 66 bottom rail capacitors (oscillator, soft-start and timing nets excluded), 56 have their ground pad more than 1 mm from the nearest stack; median 1.61 mm. Each ground pad has 1 microvia (4 on 0805 bulk capacitors). With L4-L13 about 1.13 mm (stackup.txt) and via radius about 0.075 mm: 4e-7 x 1.13e-3 x ln(1.6/0.075) = 1.38 nH, against 0.86 nH with a ground via 0.5 mm away. A 470 nF capacitor's resonance moves from about 8-10 MHz to about 5-7 MHz.
findings.source: AMD UG483 7 Series FPGAs PCB Design Guide, chapter 2 (capacitor placement and mounting inductance), https://docs.amd.com/v/u/en-US/ug483_7Series_PCB ; AMD UG482 for GTP supply noise. Neither could be opened for this review (the AMD URL returned 404); the numbers are engineering judgement.
findings.consequence: Supply noise in roughly the 5-50 MHz band is somewhat higher than the capacitor count suggests, most importantly on the GTP supplies, where noise turns into transmit jitter.
findings.suggested_action: Give the ground pad of each GTP supply capacitor (C51-C56), and of the worst VCCINT and VCCAUX capacitors, its own nearby full ground stack, then re-check the distances.

findings.what: A few slow nets were routed as short 'hop' tracks inside the L2 and L13 ground pours, which cuts narrow slots in those planes. findings.title: No record sets the GTP cable line rate, and the only stated figure, 1.25 Gb/s, cannot carry eight ASICs.
findings.what: Each Frontend sends the data of eight ASICs over one transceiver (GTP) lane in the HDMI cable: 1.536 Gb/s of payload with packed 12-bit samples, or 2.048 Gb/s with 16-bit words. After line coding (8b/10b adds 25 %, 64B/66B about 3 %) and with the 125 MHz reference, that needs 2.0 Gb/s (64B/66B), 2.5 Gb/s (8b/10b, packed 12-bit) or 3.125 Gb/s (8b/10b, 16-bit words, which the weekly deck's 2 GB/s for 64 ASICs implies). The only records that state a rate, the HDMI design inputs and the power estimate, assume about 1.25 Gb/s because they counted one ASIC per port. The hardware supports every candidate rate and the HDMI board's recording-lane routing does not depend on the 1.25 Gb/s figure, so what is open is the rate decision and a cable loss check at that rate.
findings.where: Frontend U1 (XC7A35T-2CSG325I) GTP TX0 H1/H2 -> J3.3/J3.5 -> about 1.8 m Micro-HDMI cable -> HDMI Extension Board J610-J617 pins 3/5 -> U801 ESD, C745-C760 AC capacitors -> MC3 GTY receivers. Reference: Y1 125 MHz LVDS on GTP REFCLK1 (B5/B6).

findings.source: AMD DS181 Artix-7 FPGAs Data Sheet v1.27.1 (3 Jul 2024), Table 52 GTP Transceiver Performance, p.51, https://docs.amd.com/v/u/en-US/ds181_Artix_7_Data_Sheet; AMD UG482 7 Series GTP Transceivers User Guide v1.9 (gearbox, PLL dividers), https://docs.amd.com/v/u/en-US/ug482_7Series_GTP_Transceivers; ASIC reference (inputs/asic/ASIC_Reference/ASIC_REFERENCE.md). findings.title: The separate SYNC pair is undriven on HDMI ports 1, 2, 7 and 8, and the Frontend cannot tell its port.
findings.what: Every Frontend is the same and always feeds cable pins 12/14 (CABLE_SYNC) into an LVDS receiver in the FPGA, with only a 100 ohm resistor across the pair and no bias resistors. The HDMI Extension Board drives these pins only on ports 3-6; on the other four ports they are left open. An LVDS receiver with 0 V between its inputs (below its 100 mV minimum) can output either level or toggle on noise. The cable carries no port number, so the gateware cannot decide on its own whether to use this pair or the SYNC folded into pins 9/11.
findings.where: Frontend FPGA Board: J3.12/J3.14 /CABLE_SYNC_P/N -> U18 clamp -> R64 100R -> U1.B9/A9 (bank 15, LVDS_25, DIFF_TERM FALSE). HDMI Extension Board: J612-J615 pins 12/14 driven (B64_L16/L23/L22/L18); J610, J611, J616, J617 pins 12/14 unconnected.
findings.evidence: exports/frontend/netlist.xml: /CABLE_SYNC_P = J3.12, R64.1, U1.B9, U18.1/10; /CABLE_SYNC_N = J3.14, R64.2, U1.A9, U18.2/9; R64 100R (parts.csv row 153); no bias resistors. XDC: B9/A9 LVDS_25 DIFF_TERM FALSE. exports/hdmi/netlist.xml: J612-J615 pins 12/14 on B64_L16P/N, L23P/N, L22P/N, L18P/N (MC1) with U811-U814 clamps; J610, J611, J616, J617 pins 12/14 'unconnected-(...-SYNC_P/N-Pad12/14)'. J3.1 only sources 1.8 V through R27. Schematic V46 note: 'port-number strap or firmware selection not defined'.
findings.source: AMD DS181 Artix-7 FPGAs Data Sheet v1.27.1 (3 Jul 2024), Table 11 LVDS_25 VIDIFF min 100 mV, VICM 0.3-1.5 V, https://docs.amd.com/v/u/en-US/ds181_Artix_7_Data_Sheet; AMD UG471 v1.10 p.92 (external termination); Engineering judgement.
findings.consequence: A Frontend on port 1, 2, 7 or 8 whose gateware uses CABLE_SYNC sees random sync pulses. No harm is done if the gateware ignores this pair there.
findings.suggested_action: Write the rule into the gateware spec (CABLE_SYNC valid only on ports 3-6, or folded SYNC on 9/11 everywhere, or a port number sent in the command stream), or add a small fail-safe bias on the Frontend side.

findings.title: Cable pairs are about 88-93 ohm instead of 100 ohm, and the JLC remark sets no impedance target.
findings.what: The six cable-pair nets (clock, command and SYNC) are routed as 0.08 mm tracks with a 0.31 mm gap, which gives about 88-90 ohm on L8 and 92-93 ohm on L10 against the 100 ohm target for HDMI cable and LVDS pairs. JLC's track-width tolerance of +/-20 % moves this by about +/-7 ohm. The JLC remark only asks JLC to report the impedance of this geometry; it states no target, so JLC will apply no impedance control. A decision is needed before upload: an order for 'controlled 100 ohm' would put the as-drawn copper at the edge of JLC's +/-10 % window.
findings.where: Frontend: /CABLE_CLK_P/N on L8 (25.25 / 25.64 mm), /CABLE_CMDSYNC_P/N on L10 (23.66 / 24.09 mm), /CABLE_SYNC_P/N on L8 (6.43 / 6.39 mm); /CABLE_SYNC_N also has 1.86 mm on L12. inputs/frontend/V3_order/JLC_ORDER_NOTES.txt, Impedance line.

Field solve (a review working file (not published)): 88.3 ohm (L8), 91.6 ohm (L10); closed-form stripline check: 88.6 / 92.3 ohm; record inputs/frontend/V3_review/impedance.json: 89.7 / 92.7 ohm, 0.15 mm-core variant 97.4 / 101.1 ohm. Sensitivity about 450-500 ohm per mm of width, so +/-0.016 mm gives about +/-7 ohm. Reflection at 90 ohm into 100 ohm: about 5 %. The remark's Tracks line names L8 / L10 / L12; its Impedance line omits the L12 piece, which is a short uncoupled single trace.
findings.source: JLCPCB HDI PCB page, impedance at 50 ohm and above held to +/-10 %, https://jlcpcb.com/pcb-fabrication/hdi-pcb ; JLCPCB PCB capabilities, track width +/-20 %, https://jlcpcb.com/capabilities/pcb-capabilities ; 100 ohm differential target for HDMI cable and LVDS (TIA/EIA-644); project routing rule G07.
findings.consequence: The roughly 5 % reflection is harmless at 125 MHz over about 25 mm if the receiver termination is right. The real risk is ordering 'controlled 100 ohm' on this copper, which JLC would treat as out of tolerance.
findings.suggested_action: Decide before upload: state about 90 ohm (as built) as the target, leave impedance control off, or take the 0.15 mm-core stack-up variant. Do not order 'controlled 100 ohm' on this copper.

findings.title: 427 stacked laser-via columns and 604 lasers on buried vias need JLC's written acceptance before ordering.
findings.what: The U1, J1 and J2 escapes are built almost entirely from stacked vias: laser-drilled microvias placed directly on top of each other and directly on the capped L4-L11 buried vias. JLC's published HDI rules do cover stacked vias, define them as aligned blind and buried vias, and offer the 3rd-order process this needs. What JLC does not publish is a limit on stack height or any reliability test or coupon, and it says staggered (offset) vias are generally preferred for yield. findings.title: The remark now asks JLC for the flatness the DF40 connectors need, but JLC has not agreed, and even 0.5 % bow allows about 0.036 mm across J1/J2.
findings.area: Board flatness at J1/J2 and U1 (fabrication requirement)
findings.what: Hirose allows at most 0.02 mm of board warpage at the centre of a DF40 connector relative to its two ends. For HDI boards JLC publishes only bow and twist of 0.75 % or less (IPC Class 2), and says 0.5 % on special request. IPC measures bow as the gap under a board edge divided by the edge length. On this 25.42 mm board, 0.75 % therefore allows a 0.19 mm gap; with an even curve that is 0.055 mm across J1/J2's 13.6 mm contact span. Neither the PCB remark nor any Frontend record states a flatness, bow/twist or warpage requirement. A board that JLC accepts can therefore still be outside the connector's rating.
findings.where: Frontend 8L V3, 14 layers V3. J1 is on the bottom, pads x 120.705-123.785, y 105.77-119.37. J2 is on the bottom, pads x 103.205-106.285, same y. Both are DF40C-70DS running along the 25.42 mm board length. U1 is on the top, 15 x 15 mm, x 108.72-123.72, y 105.5-120.5, directly over J1. Order remark: inputs/frontend/V3_order/JLC_ORDER_NOTES.txt, PCB remark lines 1-14.
findings.evidence:
Conversion assumes an even (circular) curve: the gap at the middle of a chord s is B x s^2 / L, for bow B measured over edge length L.
- 0.75 % over L = 25.42 mm: 0.0546 mm over the 13.6 mm contact span; 0.0813 mm over the 16.6 mm DF40C-70DS body; 0.0664 mm over U1's 15 mm along y (0.0747 mm along the 22.59 mm x edge).
- 0.5 %: 0.036 / 0.054 / 0.044 mm for the same spans.
- JLC's blog divides by the 34.01 mm diagonal instead, which gives 0.041 mm over 13.6 mm.
- Holding 0.020 mm over 13.6 mm needs bow of 0.275 % or less on the single board (0.184 % for 16.6 mm).
- In a 70 mm assembly panel at 0.75 %, the same curvature gives 0.0198 mm over 13.6 mm.
- Twist at 0.75 % (gap 2 x 34.01 x 0.0075 = 0.51 mm) would lift one corner of J1's 3.78 x 13.6 mm footprint 0.046 mm off the plane of the other three.
JLC_ORDER_NOTES.txt: the only 'flat' is line 7 (via-in-pad). A grep of all text files under inputs/frontend finds no warpage, bow, twist, thieving or copper-balance text. FPGA-LDO A's inputs/ldo_a/V12_order/JLC_Remarks_paste.txt is also silent. Script: a review working file (not published)

findings.title: JTAG reaches the FPGA only through the HDMI cable, with no test pads and no ESD clamp at either cable end.
findings.what: JTAG is the four-wire programming and debug port (TCK, TMS, TDI, TDO). On the Frontend these four lines run straight from the Micro-HDMI connector J3 to the FPGA, with no ESD clamp (a part that diverts static discharge), no series resistor and no test pad. The cable's LVDS pairs are clamped by U17/U18, yet two spare U18 channels are tied to GND, and the HDMI Extension Board has only 100 ohm resistors on these lines, so neither end clamps JTAG. The only way to program or probe a Frontend is through the cable, the HDMI board's U611 switch and its USB-JTAG.
findings.where: Frontend FPGA Board: J3.17 FPGA_JTAG_TCK -> U1.F8, J3.2 TMS -> U1.R8, J3.15 TDI -> U1.T9, J3.18 TDO -> U1.T8; J3.1 CABLE_TARGET_SENSE -> R27 (1k to VCCAUX_1V8); U18 pins 4-7 (IO3/IO4) on GND. HDMI Extension Board: J610 pins 17/15/18/2 -> R640-R643 -> U611 (same on all ports).
findings.evidence: exports/frontend/netlist.xml: each of FPGA_JTAG_TCK/TMS/TDI/TDO has exactly two nodes (J3 pin, U1 ball). TP1-TP14 sit only on rails, GND, BOOT_RAILS_PG, INIT_B and DONE. U18 pins 4/5/6/7 on GND; its field says unused IO3/IO4 are tied to GND. exports/hdmi/netlist.xml: HDMI1_JTAG_TCK/TDI/TDO/TMS = J610 pin + R640/R641/R643/R642 only, far ends to U611 NO4/NO6/NO5/NO3. TCK and TDO use cable pins 17/18 (the HDMI SCL/SDA wires, not a shielded pair); crosstalk between them is plausible but unproven, and the cable length is not in the files.
findings.source: AMD UG470 7 Series FPGAs Configuration User Guide v1.17 (5 Dec 2023), Table 2-4 (TCK), https://docs.amd.com/v/u/en-US/ug470_7Series_Config; TI TPD4E02B04 SLVSD85B, as used on the cable LVDS lines, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tpd4e02b04.pdf; Engineering judgement on ESD and bench access.
findings.consequence: A discharge while plugging the cable lands directly on bank 0, which also holds the configuration pins, and relies only on the FPGA's on-chip protection. If the HDMI board or cable path has a fault, a new Frontend cannot be programmed or probed at all.
findings.suggested_action: Decide whether to accept this. If not, add JTAG test pads (with GND and 1.8 V) and clamp J3 pins 2/15/17/18, using the two spare U18 channels for TCK and TMS plus a second low-capacitance array like U17.

findings.title: VIN_5V from the cable reaches U16 with no clamp, and hot-plug overshoot against its 6.5 V limit is unmeasured.
findings.what: The 5 V from the HDMI cable goes straight to the input and enable pins of U16, the buck module that feeds every other rail. The only parts on that net are two 22 uF capacitors, one 100 nF capacitor and a test point; there is no TVS diode or other clamp. Plugging a cable into a live port can make the voltage ring above 5 V for a moment, because the cable's inductance and the ceramic capacitors form a lightly damped circuit. The current-limit switch on the HDMI board side should help damp this, but nobody has measured it, so the files cannot settle whether the peak stays below U16's 6.5 V absolute maximum; a scope capture at the first plug-in would.
findings.where: Frontend: J3.19 -> net VIN_5V -> U16 pins 13, 14 (IN) and pin 4 (EN); C206, C207 (22 uF / 10 V, 0805), C209 (100 nF, 0201), TP14. HDMI Extension Board side: net PORT1_5V, U701 (TPS2553DBVR) with C721 (1 uF) at J610.19.
findings.evidence: exports/frontend/netlist.xml net VIN_5V: C206.1, C207.1, C209.1, J3.19, TP14.1, U16.4/13/14 only; parts.csv has no D* part on it. parts.csv: C206/C207 GRM21BR61A226ME44L, C209 GRM033R61A104KE15D. MPM3833C datasheet p3: every pin except SW -0.3 to +6.5 V absolute maximum; VIN 2.75-6 V recommended. Source voltage 5.02 V (U700, HDMI board), leaving 1.48 V (30 %) to 6.5 V. exports/hdmi/netlist.xml PORT1_5V: U701.6, C721 1 uF, J610.19, TP701. Schematic V46 U16 note marks hot-plug overshoot as unverified.
findings.source: MPS MPM3833C datasheet Rev 1.0, p3, Absolute Maximum Ratings and Recommended Operating Conditions, https://www.monolithicpower.com (MPM3833C product page); engineering judgement for the hot-plug ringing.
findings.consequence: If the plug-in ringing is under-damped, for example with a short, thick cable, the peak could pass 6.5 V and damage U16, which would take down every rail on the board.
findings.suggested_action: On the first board, scope VIN_5V at TP14 while plugging the real cable into a live HDMI board port, using the shortest planned cable. If there is spare area, add a DNP TVS footprint on VIN_5V and fit it if the peak exceeds 6 V.

findings.title: Four pull-ups are outside the values AMD and TI specify: PROGRAM_B, INIT_B and FCS_B use 4.99 kOhm where UG470 asks for 4.7 kOhm or less, and the TPS74801 power-good node uses 4.99 kOhm where TI requires 10 kOhm to 1 MOhm.
findings.what: UG470 asks for a pull-up of 4.7 kOhm or less on PROGRAM_B and INIT_B (to VCCO_0) and on FCS_B (to VCCO_14). The board uses 4.99 kOhm on all three (R17, R18, R19), and the morning review recorded these pins as matching UG470. TI says the TPS74801 power-good (PG) pull-up must be 10 kOhm to 1 MOhm, because the pin is meant to sink no more than 1 mA; R9 on BOOT_RAILS_PG_3V3 is 4.99 kOhm. None of these is expected to cause a failure: the configuration pull-ups are about 6 % weaker than AMD's limit (INIT_B edge time constant near 75 ns), and R9 sinks about 0.60-0.66 mA, below 1 mA. The PG low level stays under U6's 0.4 V enable-low limit, but by only about 0.1 V at TI's 1 mA rating with the older TPS74801 chip, which the JLC BOM may deliver (FE-18).
findings.where: Frontend: R17 FPGA_PROGRAM_B (U1.P10) to VCCAUX_1V8; R18 FPGA_INIT_B (U1.T10) to VCCAUX_1V8; R19 FPGA_QSPI_CS_N (U1.L15, FCS_B) to VCCO_1V5; all bottom. R9 BOOT_RAILS_PG_3V3 (U5.3 PG) to VIN_3V3, top; the node also carries U4.12 PG, U6.5 EN, U12.3 MR and TP10. All four are RC0201FR-074K99L.
findings.evidence: exports/frontend/netlist.xml and parts.csv: R9, R17, R18 and R19 are 4.99k RC0201FR-074K99L (1 %) between the rails and nets above. UG470 Table 2-4: PROGRAM_B and INIT_B '<= 4.7 kOhm pull-up resistor to VCCO_0' (p21); FCS_B '<= 4.7 kOhm pull-up resistor to VCCO_14' (p27). TPS748: PG pull-up must be 10 kOhm to 1 MOhm, sink up to 1 mA (sec. 6.3.2 p17); IPG absolute maximum 1.5 mA (p4); PG low <= 0.3 V at 1 mA for the legacy chip and <= 0.125 V for the new chip; VEN(lo) <= 0.4 V (sec. 5.5, pp6-7). R9 current: 3.3 V / 4.99 kOhm = 0.66 mA; (3.315 - 0.3 V) / 4.99 kOhm = 0.60 mA. INIT_B edge: about 15 pF (8 pF pin + U11 + trace and TP11) x 5 kOhm = 75 ns. This contradicts the known/frontend.json checked_ok item 'Configuration mode and pins', which calls the 4.99 kOhm pull-ups compliant citing UG470 Tables 2-3/2-4.
findings.source: AMD UG470 7 Series FPGAs Configuration User Guide v1.17 (5 Dec 2023), Table 2-4, p.21 (PROGRAM_B, INIT_B: 4.7 kOhm or less to VCCO_0) and p.27 (FCS_B: 4.7 kOhm or less to VCCO_14), https://docs.amd.com/api/khub/documents/FOs3lXmlcWxBhTIFxVKyGA/content ; TI TPS748 data sheet SBVS074N (Jun 2024), sec. 6.3.2 p.17 (PG pull-up 10 kOhm-1 MOhm, sink 1 mA or less), sec. 5.1 p.4 (IPG absolute maximum), sec. 5.5 pp.6-7 (VEN(lo), VPG(lo) for legacy and new chip), https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps74801.pdf
findings.consequence: A failure is unlikely, but the board does not follow two datasheets the records cite, which a later review or AMD support would flag. The configuration lines get slightly weaker pull-ups than AMD specifies, and the PG node uses a stronger pull-up than TI's stated range, with about 0.1 V margin on U6's enable-low threshold if the legacy chip is fitted.
findings.suggested_action: At the next schematic edit, before ordering, change R17, R18 and R19 to 4.7 kOhm in the same 0201 footprint (for example RT0201BRD074K7L, JLC C852254, in stock); no copper change is needed. Changing R9 to 10 kOhm meets TI's stated range; it is optional, since R9's 0.60-0.66 mA is already within TI's 1 mA limit.
findings.relation: new (contradicts the known/frontend.json checked_ok item 'Configuration mode and pins')

findings.title: MGTAVTT power-good is not used, so configuration can start without MGTAVTT being confirmed good.
findings.what: MGTAVTT is the 1.2 V supply for the FPGA transceiver (GTP) terminations. The GTP termination calibration runs only once, during configuration, and needs every transceiver supply valid beforehand. U6 (MGTAVTT) has its power-good pin unconnected and is enabled by the same node that releases the reset supervisor U12, so configuration waits for VCCO_1V5 and MGTAVCC but not for MGTAVTT. It works by timing margin: the supervisor delay is at least ten times U6's soft-start ramp, so only a slow or failed U6 would be missed.
findings.where: Frontend FPGA Board: U6 (TPS74801, MGTAVTT_1V2) pin 3 PG unconnected; U6.5 EN on BOOT_RAILS_PG_3V3 = wired-AND of U4.12 PG (VCCO_1V5) and U5.3 PG (MGTAVCC), also U12.3 MR (TPS389001), R9, TP10; C50 10 nF soft-start on U6.7; C84 1 uF on U12 CT; U12.6 BOOT_RESET_N to U11 (PROGRAM_B / INIT_B) and U14. MGTAVTT_1V2 feeds U1 A2/C1/E1/F3/G2.
findings.evidence: exports/frontend/netlist.xml for all connections. U6 soft-start: 10 nF x 0.8 V / 440 nA = 18 ms (legacy die), or 15 ms at 530 nA (new die). U12 delay: 1.07 s/uF x 1 uF = 1.07 s nominal, about 0.2-0.27 s if the 0402 X6S C84 derates to the 250 nF the record allows. Ramp is inside the DS181 TMGTAVTT limit of 0.2-50 ms.
findings.source: AMD UG482 7 Series FPGAs GTP Transceivers User Guide v1.9 (19 Dec 2016), p.219, https://docs.amd.com/v/u/en-US/ug482_7Series_GTP_Transceivers; TI TPS748 data sheet SBVS074N p.6 (I_SS, VREF, Eq. 2), https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps74801.pdf; TI TPS3890 data sheet SLVSD65A (tPD vs CCT, MR behaviour); AMD DS181 v1.27.1 Table 7.
findings.consequence: A faulty or slow MGTAVTT would give a configured FPGA with badly calibrated GTP termination instead of an FPGA held in reset.
findings.suggested_action: On a later spin, join U6 PG to BOOT_RAILS_PG_3V3 with the existing pull-up; no change is needed for a first build.

findings.title: At the worst-case low 1.5 V I/O rail, the cable LVDS inputs keep only about 24 mV of DC margin.
findings.what: The cable clock, command and SYNC pairs arrive as LVDS (low-voltage differential signalling) into FPGA banks powered at 1.5 V (VCCO_1V5). The FPGA data sheet recommends that an input never goes higher than VCCO + 0.2 V. With U4 at its worst-case low output and the XEM at its worst-case high common mode (the average of the two wires) and swing, the input high level stays below that limit by only about 24 mV. The limit is still met at these stacked worst cases, typical parts leave about 0.3 V, and short excursions above it do not damage the input, so this is a margin observation to confirm at bring-up.
findings.where: Frontend FPGA Board: U4 (MPM3833C, VCCO_1V5) with divider R7 150k / R8 100k (0.1 %); U1 balls P14/R15 (CABLE_CLK) and M14/N14 (CABLE_CMDSYNC) in bank 14, B9/A9 (CABLE_SYNC) in bank 15; LVDS_25 inputs with DIFF_TERM FALSE and external 100 ohm terminations R61/R62/R64 (bottom).
findings.evidence: U4 worst-case low output: 0.591 V x (1 + 150k x 0.999 / (100k x 1.001)) = 1.476 V, so the recommended ceiling is 1.676 V (MPM3833C VFB 591-609 mV; R7/R8 from exports/frontend/parts.csv). XEM worst-case high level: VOCM 1.425 V + 0.454 V / 2 = 1.652 V (DS931 VOCM max 1.425 V, VODIFF max 454 mV). DC margin about 24 mV (25.5 mV if resistor tolerance is ignored). Typical case (VOCM 1.25 V, VCCO 1.50 V): about 0.3 V. Pin standards from inputs/frontend/V2_review_fixes/Frontend_V46_pins_V2.xdc. The MPM3833C 100 mV p-p load-transient figure (p5) is for a 0-2 A step at 1.2 V output and does not describe this lightly loaded rail.
findings.source: AMD DS181 Artix-7 Data Sheet v1.27.1, Table 2 (VIN recommended max VCCO + 0.20 V); AMD UG471 7 Series SelectIO v1.10, pp.91-93, Table 1-44, https://docs.amd.com/api/khub/documents/IbGcnPFe6eF19RHma_Y~IA/content; MPS MPM3833C Rev 1.0, pp.4-5, https://www.monolithicpower.com/en/documentview/productdocument/index/version/2/document_type/Datasheet/lang/en/sku/MPM3833CGRH-Z/document_id/4426/; Opal Kelly / AMD DS931 LVDS DC table v1.8. DS181 and DS931 were read only through AMD search summaries because the direct pages returned 404.
findings.consequence: Only a unit at the combined low-VCCO, high-common-mode corner would sit near the recommended input limit; no damage is expected. No margin is left for an error in the assumed figures.
findings.suggested_action: At bring-up, measure the XEM LVDS common mode and the single-ended high level at R61/R62/R64 against VCCO_1V5. Trimming U4 higher is possible but also raises the ASIC's 1.5 V I/O supply, so do it only if the measurement and the ASIC limits allow.

findings.title: The ASIC designer confirmed 1.5 V logic with Schmitt-trigger inputs, but its input and output voltage figures are still not on record.
findings.what: Every ASIC-facing FPGA pin uses LVCMOS15, a 1.5 V logic standard, matching the ASIC's 1.5 V digital supply (DVDD). The FPGA side is known: it reads below 35 % of VCCO as low and above 65 % as high, and drives below 25 % and above 75 %. No document in the workspace gives the ASIC's switching levels, output levels, load, clamp or limits when unpowered, so the files cannot show that each side meets the other's levels. Only the ASIC designer's figures would settle it.
findings.where: Frontend FPGA Board U1 banks 14, 15 and 34 on VCCO_1V5; ASIC lines and control lines on J1/J2.
findings.evidence: inputs/frontend/V2_review_fixes/Frontend_V46_pins_V2.xdc: 110 single-ended ports LVCMOS15 (including the non-ASIC CLK25_PL, STIM_START_SHARED and EN_GTPWR_1V5) and 6 LVDS_25. exports/frontend/netlist.xml: every U1 VCCO ball other than E10/R10 on VCCO_1V5. inputs/asic/ASIC_Reference/ASIC_REFERENCE.md line 175 (U03): ASIC VIH/VIL/VOH/VOL, loading, clamp and powered-off limits absent; lines 34 and 130: DVDD 1.5 V. DS181 Table 8 LVCMOS15: VIL max 35 % VCCO, VIH min 65 % VCCO, VOL max 25 % VCCO, VOH min 75 % VCCO.
findings.source: ASIC_REFERENCE.md U03; AMD DS181 Artix-7 Data Sheet v1.27.1, Table 8, pp.9-10 (LVCMOS15 row).
findings.consequence: If the ASIC pads switch at a different fraction of DVDD, or DVDD and VCCO_1V5 drift apart, there could be data errors or extra current in the ASIC pad ring.
findings.suggested_action: Ask the ASIC designer for VIH/VIL/VOH/VOL at DVDD = 1.5 V and the allowed pin voltage with DVDD off.

findings.title_was: The ASIC's input and output voltage levels are unknown, so the 1.5 V interface cannot be closed.

findings.title: Y2's datasheet covers only a 15 pF load, so its drive into the 830 Ohm level-shift divider is not specified.
findings.what: The 25 MHz oscillator Y2 drives R44 (150 Ohm) and R63 (680 Ohm) in series to ground. This shifts its 1.8 V swing to about 1.47 V for the 1.5 V bank. The YXC datasheet gives only a 15 pF CMOS load and VOH of at least 90 % of VDD, with no output current or output resistance, while the divider draws about 2 mA at high level. A normal CMOS output leaves wide margin; T14 would miss a high only if Y2's output resistance were above about 370 Ohm.
findings.where: Frontend: Y2 OT201625MJBA4SL (bottom) pin 3 /CLK25_RAW, R44 150 Ohm, CLK25_PL (U1.T14 MRCC, LVCMOS15), R63 680 Ohm to GND; Y2 VDD /CLK25_VDD from VCCAUX_1V8 through L3.

findings.title: Three Frontend mirror-layer pairs differ by 72-75 points of copper, outside JLC's balance guidance, but the bow this causes across J1/J2 is under 1 um nominal and about 4-6 um at worst.
findings.what:
A multilayer board stays flattest when each layer's copper matches its mirror layer about the board centre. Adding the L5/L6 signal layers left three pairs unbalanced:
- L3 power, 80 %, against L12 signal, 8 %.
- L7 ground, 82 %, against L8 signal, 8 %.
- L6 signal, 7 %, against L9 ground, 82 %. This pair bends the other way and cancels part of the first two.
Laminate theory (a layer-by-layer bending calculation) gives about 0.2-0.4 um across J1/J2. With every material value at its worst it gives at most about 4 um, or 6 um over the full 16.6 mm body. The bow is small because the board is only 25 mm long and 1.57 mm thick, and because copper expands almost as much as the laminate does. The result is 5 to 80 times under Hirose's 0.02 mm, so the imbalance alone does not justify a copper change.
findings.where: Frontend 8L V3, 14 layers V3: whole board (574.24 mm2) and three windows: J1 (x 120.7-123.8, y 105.7-119.5), J2 (x 103.2-106.3, same y) and U1 (x 108.7-123.7, y 105.5-120.5). The mid-plane is the 0.100 mm core between L7 and L8.
findings.evidence:
Method: copper is the pcbnew union of filled zones, tracks, pads and via lands per layer (cu_area.py -> fe_cu_area.json), clipped to the outline. The order Gerbers, rasterised at 2.5 um (gerber_area.py -> fe_gerber_area.json), agree within +0.8 to +1.6 mm2 per layer.
Mirror pairs (% copper): L1/L14 25.6/22.1; L2/L13 83.6/83.5; L3/L12 79.9/8.4; L4/L11 75.2/81.9; L5/L10 7.9/9.8; L6/L9 6.5/81.9; L7/L8 81.9/8.1.
Halves: L1-L7 hold 2,070 mm2 and L8-L14 1,697 mm2 (Gerbers: 2,078 / 1,705). Copper volume is 62.8 / 51.5 mm3. The net moment-weighted imbalance, sum(df x t x z), is 0.0091 mm2, which is 54 % of a full L3/L12 swap.
Windows (J1 / J2 / U1):
- L3/L12: 84.0/15.5, 89.3/3.3, 84.1/12.8.
- L6/L9: 9.8/84.0, 3.8/90.4, 10.6/83.9.
- L7/L8: 84.0/7.1, 90.4/14.5, 83.9/10.7.
Lamination theory (clt_warp.py; it reproduces Timoshenko's bimetal formula exactly, tools/clt_selftest.py):
- Nominal curvature is 1.0e-5 per mm (radius 96 m), which gives 0.24 um over 13.6 mm.
- Sweep of 4,374 cases: copper 70-130 GPa and 16.5-17.7 ppm/K; resin 2.5-4.5 GPa and 50-70 ppm/K; laminate 14-26 GPa and 11-18 ppm/K; three mixing rules; dT -145 and -175 K.
- Worst cases over 13.6 mm: 2.4 um (whole board), 2.4 um (J1 window), 3.8 um (J2 window). Over 16.6 mm: 5.6 um (J2 window). Over 15 mm: 2.6 um (U1 window).
- Reflow case (resin above Tg, dT +30 to +65 K): 1.0 um or less over 13.6 mm.
- Reaching Hirose's limit needs a curvature of 8.65e-4 per mm (radius 1.16 m).
All files are in a review working file (not published)
findings.source:
Hirose DF40 catalogue (1 Jun 2024), p21. https://www.hirose.com/en/product/series/DF40
JLCPCB blog 'Copper Balancing in PCBs', 12 Jun 2026: 40-60 % per layer; below 30 % needs extensive thieving; mirrored layers within 15-20 %, attributed to IPC-6012. https://jlcpcb.com/blog/pcb-copper-balancing
JLCPCB blog 'PCB Warpage Control', updated 29 Oct 2026: under 30 % top/bottom variation. https://jlcpcb.com/blog/pcb-warpage-control
JLCPCB HDI page (laminate S1000-2M or NP-175F, Tg 170 C). https://jlcpcb.com/pcb-fabrication/hdi-pcb
Shengyi S1000-2M data sheet CN-TDS-2308-04, p1: Tg 180-185 C; no in-plane CTE or modulus. Copy hosted by PCBWay: https://pcbwayfile.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/web/240405/CN-TDS-2308-04-S1000-2M-S1000-2MB-OK.pdf
Method: classical lamination theory, checked against Timoshenko's bimetal formula. Copper, epoxy and in-plane laminate property ranges are from memory, not re-read.
findings.consequence: Copper balance is not a reason to re-spin or to add fill for flatness. The model covers thermal mismatch only. It does not cover resin cure shrinkage, glass-weave stress, the three sequential HDI laminations or soldered parts, which is why a first-article flatness check is still worth doing.
findings.suggested_action:
Make no copper change for flatness. If the pin map V6 re-spin adds fill anyway to meet JLC's guidance:
- Prefer GND fill on L12, stitched by 11-12 and 12-13 lasers and kept at least 0.2 mm from lanes. This adds L11-L13 ground joins that help FE-10 and FE-21, at the cost of more lasers (FE-11).
- Keep fill at least 0.5 mm from the CABLE_* pairs on L8/L10 (FE-22).
- Remember that fill on L5/L6/L8/L10 can reach ground only through the L4-L11 buried GND vias.
Re-run cu_area.py and clt_warp.py after any change.

findings.area: Mating boards: copper balance and DF40 flatness
findings.what: On FPGA-LDO A V12 and on the Option B LDO board V2, the L2 AGND plane (74 % and 82 % copper) faces a 16-17 % L5 signal layer. Laminate theory puts the resulting bend across their DF40s at under 1 um nominal and 2-6 um at worst over 13.6-15.6 mm, so copper balance needs no change. The Option B router is balanced. findings.title: A configured XEM can drive the cable LVDS pairs into the Frontend before its 1.5 V I/O rail is up.
findings.what: The cable clock, command and SYNC pairs use LVDS (low-voltage differential signalling, a pair of wires held near 1.2 V that carry a small current difference) and run straight from J3 to FPGA pins with nothing to disconnect them. The Frontend's 1.5 V supply for that FPGA I/O bank (VCCO_1V5) comes up last, after 5 V, 3.3 V and the core rail, and is off whenever a port's 5 V switch on the HDMI Extension Board is off. In that window the XEM drives about 1.2 V into an unpowered bank, so current flows through the FPGA's input clamp diodes (protection diodes to the supply rail). The FPGA allows up to 10 mA per pin this way even when unpowered, but the XEM driver current and the back-feed into VCCO_1V5 have not been measured or taken from the XEM documentation.

findings.title: The GT pair is P/N swapped by design; the Frontend pin file now records the inversion, but no HDMI Extension Board file does.
findings.what: The recording data travel on one differential pair, a P wire and an N wire. On the Frontend, cable pin 3 carries N and pin 5 carries P, while on all eight HDMI Extension Board ports pin 3 goes to the receiver's P input and pin 5 to N, so a straight cable delivers inverted data. This is intended: gateware must set TXPOLARITY = 1 on the Frontend transmitter and must not also invert on the XEM receiver. The requirement is written in the Frontend schematic note (V42), the HDMI V35 review and the HDMI V36 record, but not in the current Frontend constraint file or any of the three HDMI constraint files; an earlier Frontend draft constraint file had it.

findings.title: Bank 14 runs at 1.5 V during configuration while bank 0 runs at 1.8 V, which UG470 says should match.
findings.what: CFGBVS is the FPGA pin that sets the allowed voltage of the configuration banks; tied low, banks 0 and 14 may each run at 1.8 V or 1.5 V, so nothing is overstressed. UG470 still says bank 14 should match bank 0 when it carries configuration pins, and its SPI table lists only matched pairs. Here bank 0 is 1.8 V and bank 14 is 1.5 V, so the flash data and chip-select pins run at 1.5 V while the flash clock runs at 1.8 V; the translator U8 makes the flash side work. Whether Vivado's CONFIG_VOLTAGE setting and design-rule check accept this mix cannot be settled from the files; one Vivado run would settle it.
